advances: Sharpness of a regression coefficient for actual whole-line covers at budgets at least one half.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Each binary base is extreme in the projection of the lifted convex hull, so its fiber consists of its own interval. Whole-line coverage with two caps requires one normal of each sign. Write their margins as $x-a(z)$ and $b(z)-x$ for affine $a,b$, with $a(z)\le b(z)$ at each binary base. Integrate the first untruncated margin on the positive-height fibers and the second on the negative-height fibers, discarding the other nonnegative hinges. This lower-bounds the total hinge by
$$
4L+\sum_{\epsilon_z=-1} b(z)-\sum_{\epsilon_z=1} a(z)\ge4L,
$$
because the opposite diagonal sums of any affine function on the binary square are equal. The horizontal pair realizes this bound with each cap of mass two and hinge $2L$. The union bound rules out $\tau<1/2$.

For the horizontal pair the maximum of the two margins on each whole line is minimized at $0$ and equals zero there. The balanced average margin is identically zero. With $r_i=0$, $\eta_z=1$ and weights $1/2$, the transported mass of each cap is two, its transported base first moment is $(1,1)$, and its transported continuous first moment is zero. The actual cap continuous moments are $2L$ and $-2L$, exactly $\Psi_i u_i$ in the respective cap. Thus the objective-one stress balances, with every contact outside the source intervals. The derivative identity follows from the constant attained value on the interior of the feasible budget range.

The caps partition the source up to null sets. The height signs are orthogonal to every affine base feature because $\sum_z\epsilon_z=0$ and $\sum_z\epsilon_z z=0$. The conditional mean of $x$ is $\epsilon_z L$ and the within-interval variance is $1/12$. These give all the displayed moments and the limiting ratio.

source_sections.locator: 4a935c6b02656f36:01 Setting and §§1–3, exact value, stress, and regression

statement:
Let $L>1/2$, and at the binary bases $z\in\{0,1\}^2$ take the intervals $K_z=[\epsilon_z L-1/2,\epsilon_z L+1/2]$, where $\epsilon_{00}=\epsilon_{11}=1$ and $\epsilon_{10}=\epsilon_{01}=-1$. These are the actual integer fibers of their lifted convex hull and have total mass $M=4$. Use exactly two caps with unit continuous normals, required to cover the whole continuous line at each binary base, and impose cap mass at most $\tau M$. Feasibility holds exactly for $\tau\ge1/2$, and the minimum total hinge is $v(\tau)=4L$ throughout that range.

The minimizing pair $x\ge0,x\le0$ has an objective-one mass and moment stress with zero cap-budget multipliers, balanced weights $(1/2,1/2)$ and contact $x=0$ at each base, and $\eta_z=1$. The identity $M\sum_i r_i=-v'(\tau)=0$ holds for $1/2<\tau<1$. The source measure $\nu$ obtained by summing the cap restrictions of mixed volume is the original mixed volume. Label its two parts by their continuous normal $U=\epsilon_z$. If $x$ is projected in $L^2(\nu)$ onto the affine base features, the prediction is identically zero. For $A=\int U^2\,d\nu$, $Q=\int xU\,d\nu$, and $R_x=\int x^2\,d\nu$,
$$
A=4,\quad Q=4L,\quad R_x=4L^2+1/3,\qquad
R_x-QA^+Q=1/3,\quad \frac{R_x}{QA^+Q}=1+\frac{1}{12L^2}.
$$
Consequently no coefficient greater than one can hold uniformly in the source regression bound $R_x\ge QA^+Q$, even within these actual minimizing whole-line covers.
title: Sharp regression coefficient at actual whole-line hinge minimizers
